questions.questionText:
A business person employs two people to make sandwiches to sell in a café.
As well as labour, which factors of production are involved in this activity?

Why might a government choose to increase spending on healthcare instead of spending on
building new roads?

options.text: The financial cost of building new roads is lower.
The opportunity cost of building new roads is lower.
The opportunity cost of spending on healthcare is lower.
The social costs of healthcare are higher.

questions.questionText:
Those on average income consume five times more calories per day than those on
the lowest incomes.
Which type of poverty is described in each of these statements?
statement 1 statement 2

In 2020, many economies were operating under their production possibility curve (PPC).
What does this statement mean?

options.text: There was a rise in the price of goods and services in many economies.
There was a significant level of unemployment of resources.
These economies lacked resources to produce more output.
These economies were producing at the most efficient point.

questions.questionText:
Which combination of terms describes a public good?
excludable rival

The formula for a good’s price elasticity of supply needs to be completed.
price elasticity of supply =
What needs to replace X and Y to complete the formula?
X Y

options.text: change in price change in quantity supplied
change in quantity supplied change in price
% change in price % change in quantity supplied
% change in quantity supplied % change in price

questions.questionText:
In a country, the total demand for vehicle fuel is price-inelastic. However, the demand for any
given brand of vehicle fuel is price-elastic.
If brand X increased its price by 10%, what would be the most likely effect?

options.text: Consumer spending on vehicle fuel would decrease.
The prices of other brands would fall.
The revenue from brand X would increase.
The revenue from other brands would increase.

questions.questionText:
A medical report that outlined the disadvantages of eating sugar caused the demand for sugar to
decrease. However, producers of sugar were not able to adjust their supply quickly and continued
producing sugar at previous levels.
What was likely to have happened in the market for sugar?

Interest rates fall.
How might this affect consumers’ saving and spending?
saving spending

Labour-intensive sectors are the main contributors to Vietnam’s economic growth.
What does this reveal about Vietnam’s economy?

options.text: Availability of labour in Vietnam is low.
Demand for products from labour-intensive sectors is low.
Price of labour in Vietnam is high.
Production of goods and services in Vietnam is mainly dependent on labour.

questions.questionText:
An information technology (IT) specialist sets up a firm that repairs computers.
Which sector and ownership are involved in this action?
sector ownership

Which term describes the situation where the owner of a coffee plantation plans a merger with a
chain of coffee shops?

The table shows a firm’s costs for producing bicycles.
number of bicycles 0 1 2 3 4 5
total cost ($) 20 30 40 50 60 70
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The average cost of producing 4 bicycles is $15.
The average fixed cost of producing 2 bicycles is $20.
The total variable cost of producing 3 bicycles is $50.

questions.questionText: What is not likely to be a conflict between government macroeconomic aims?

options.text: economic growth and balance of payments stability
redistribution of income and full employment

questions.questionText: What will reduce income inequality?

A government decides to increase the rate of growth of domestic production through
expansionary fiscal policy.
Which combination of measures will it use?

options.text: decrease the money supply and increase the rate of interest
increase the money supply and decrease the rate of interest
decrease taxes and increase government expenditure
increase taxes and decrease government expenditure

questions.questionText:
What is the link between a change in the interest rate and investment?
interest rate investment

Which two types of citizens are counted in the calculation of the unemployment rate?
type 1 type 2

options.text: full-time student unemployed and not willing to work
unemployed and willing to work employed

questions.questionText:
An economy has a budget deficit and a high rate of inflation.
What is likely to be the consequence of a rise in unemployment?
budget deficit inflation rate

The graph shows what happened to the rate of inflation in Chad for the period from March to
December.
rate of inflation
(%)
Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec
Which statement about the general price level in Chad over this period is correct?

options.text: It was at its highest in March.
It was at its lowest in October.
It was at its lowest in December.
It was unchanged between March and April.

questions.questionText:
The Human Development Index (HDI) is one indicator of a country’s living standards.
What is included in the HDI?

options.text: birth rate, unemployment rate, number of schools
death rate, inflation rate, mean years of education
life expectancy, income per head, mean years of education
life expectancy, total GDP, number of schools

questions.questionText: What is usually found in a low-income country when comparing it with a high-income country?

options.text: a larger agricultural sector and less subsistence farming
lower levels of productivity of capital and higher levels of productivity of labour
relatively faster growth of population and an older average age
relatively lower levels of saving and a less skilled workforce

questions.questionText:
A country removes all tariffs on imported goods.
What is a benefit of this change to consumers?

A person in country X receives a dividend payment on shares that they hold in a firm in
country Y.
In which section of the current account of the balance of payments for country X will this dividend
appear?

India is now a major centre of the world computer industry. Profit margins are high since labour
costs are a tenth of those in the US.’
What does this suggest is the reason for companies locating in India rather than in the US?

The UK wants to increase exports to the US.
Which action will most likely achieve this?

options.text: borrowing US dollars from international banks
devaluing UK pounds against the US dollar
placing a quota on imports from the US
